subject: Executive briefing + next steps: CorpHealth inference pilot
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Gray <alyssa.gray@corphealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Executive briefing + next steps: CorpHealth inference pilot

Thanks for your time earlier, Alyssa — great conversation. I wanted to capture a concise executive-friendly recap, confirm the priority items we agreed on, and spell out immediate next steps so your procurement and security teams have a clean handoff.

Summary of pain / business drivers (what surfaced on the call):
- Unpredictable inference latency on current vendor endpoints leading to degraded clinician UX (spikes during peak hours).
- Rising per-request costs as throughput scales; need predictable unit economics for the pilot and production.
- Regulatory/compliance constraints: PHI in prompts, mandatory audit logging, and SSO + SCIM for teams.
- Appetite to test a VPC/private deployment or a dedicated tenancy model to meet internal security needs.

Desired outcomes (executive level):
- Pilot demonstrating stable 95th percentile latency under your peak workload and a 30% unit-cost reduction vs current baseline.
- Clear procurement path to production: SOW -> PO -> (30/60) day billing; target production decision in Q1 2027.

Risks / open questions you flagged:
- SOC2 evidence and encryption key control for PHI.
- Legal review timeline for our standard DPA + data residency addendum.
- Decision-maker alignment on budget — you mentioned pulling in finance/CFO.

Operational next steps (owners & timing):
1) Security packet: Redwood to share SOC2 snapshot, encryption and logging architecture, and a short KMS diagram. (Owner: Markus; ETA: Mon 10/05)
2) Draft SOW for a 6-week pilot (scope, success metrics, acceptance criteria, SLAs). (Owner: Marissa; ETA: Tue 10/06)
3) Procurement handshake: Evan / procurement to confirm preferred contracting flow (PO vs. PSA) and billing term preferences. (Owner: Evan / Alyssa; ETA: Tue 10/06)
4) Exec sync: 30-minute follow-up briefing for sponsors to review SOW and timeline. Proposed windows: 10/12 or 10/13. (Owner: Neha; ETA: identify slot by 10/07)

Attachments we will send with the follow-up: redwood_SOC2_snapshot_2026Q2.pdf, corphealth_proposed_sow_v1.docx, pilot_pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx

If this aligns with your read, Alyssa, we’ll proceed on the items above and loop in Evan and your procurement team. Happy to join a quick call to walk the SOW with execs.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks, Neha — this is crystal clear and helpful. A couple of clarifications from the sponsor side:
- Top priority is patient safety / deterministic responses for triage flows; any model fallback behavior must be auditable.
- We will need SSO (SAML/SCIM) and immutable audit logs for all prompt/response flows touching PHI.
- I will loop in our Head of Finance (CC next email) if the SOW looks like it aligns to a predictable monthly run rate.

Please proceed with the security packet and SOW as outlined. 10/12 or 10/13 works for a 30-minute exec review — I prefer mornings.

Alyssa
VP Product, CorpHealth

Appreciate the recap. A few procurement-level questions to speed review:
1) Contract vehicle: do you accept a PO against a SOW + MSA, or do you require DocuSign signature first?
2) Payment terms: standard Net30? Are there discounts tied to committed monthly volumes after pilot?
3) Insurance & indemnity: can you provide your certificate of insurance and confirm any standard cyber addendum?

If you can share a brief procurement checklist with the SOW, that will help us route internally.

Evan Cho
CorpHealth | Procurement Operations
procurement@corphealth.com
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Cho <evan.cho@corphealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Executive briefing + next steps: CorpHealth inference pilot

Evan — thanks for the questions. Quick answers and what we’ll attach for procurement: 
- Contract vehicle: We can do either PO against an SOW (preferred) or DocuSign; many enterprise customers choose PO+SOW to onboard quickly.
- Payment terms: Standard Net30. We can include a volume-tiered discount schedule tied to committed monthly throughput after pilot (we'll propose tiers in the pricing sheet).
- Insurance: attaching our certificate plus a summary cyber addendum; happy to engage legal on any carve-outs.

Attachments included in this email thread (stubs): redwood_SOC2_snapshot_2026Q2.pdf, corphealth_proposed_sow_v1.docx, pilot_pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx

Proposed pilot kickoff: week of 10/25 with a 6-week execution window, acceptance criteria tied to (1) 95th percentile latency under simulated peak, (2) integration of SSO/SCIM, (3) audit log ingestion into CorpHealth SIEM.
